note: Establish a six-column blend-producing baseline, with product values high enough to justify separation while keeping stage counts and reflux moderate.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a light-end-first sequence selling C3, C4, C5, C6-paraffin and C6-naphthene blends; assess purity and cost, then tune cuts/reflux and consider C7-C9 recovery. Step 1: baseline six columns.
The C3 blend needs ethane removed (>95% C3). Cuts are C3-/C4+, C4/C5+, C5/C6+, C6 paraffins/naphthenes+, then naphthenes/C7+. Moderate stages and reflux avoid excessive cost in this expensive scenario. Root runs at 12 bar to reduce light-end refrigeration; heavier columns retain most feed pressure.

note: Sharpen the C5/C6 root and downstream group cuts, and add an ethane column so the C3 blend can be sold.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a light-end-first sequence selling C3, C4, C5, C6-paraffin and C6-naphthene blends; sharpen all component-group cuts, then tune the expensive columns and C7-C9 recovery. Step 2: sharpen the full backbone and add ethane removal.
The first baseline failed because every split was too sloppy: C5 leaked both ways at the root and C4 leaked into the C5 stream. Higher reflux/boil-up and stages should unlock most blend value. Root at 13.4 bar limits refrigeration. TT now removes ethane so its bottoms can qualify as C3 mix; TTB is the C4 blend. Heavy sequence separates C6 paraffins, C6 naphthenes, heptane, octane and nonane.

note: Adopt the lean C4-first backbone and sharpen the C5/C6 and C6-paraffin/heavy cuts to unlock the three largest blend revenues.
notebook:
PLAN: Use the lean R19 C4-first backbone, sharply isolate C5 and C6-paraffin blends, then add only profitable light/heavy finishing columns. Step 1: validate the three high-value blends and measure costs.
R19 is much better than my root: C4 mix already sells for $172.5M/yr with only 4 columns and cost $478M. Its B split is too sloppy (C5 top only 62%); increasing B to 60/5/5 should recover nearly all C5 overhead. BB already puts most C6 paraffins overhead; 70/6/5 should reduce naphthene leakage. Avoid my prior full-purity tree: its $860M cost and zero sales show that many broad columns are uneconomic.

note: Adopt R29's much leaner C4-first backbone and sharpen only the C5 and C6-paraffin cuts, which should unlock about $1.45B/yr of additional blend revenue.
notebook:
PLAN: Use the lean R29 C4-first backbone, sharply isolate C5 and C6-paraffin blends, then add only profitable finishing columns. Step 1: validate the three high-value blends and measure costs.
R29 is much better than my root: C4 sells $172.5M and C3 $53.8M with only 5 columns costing $444M. Its B top is only 70% C5; increase B to 70/5/3 to reject C6 and residual C4. Its BB top is diluted by C5, so a cleaner B should also make BB's C6-paraffin cut viable; use 70/6/4. Avoid my broad full-purity tree: $914M cost and no sales.

note: The two unsold blend cuts are worth about $1.34B/yr. Sharpen both aggressively enough to cross their 95% thresholds while retaining the proven C3/C4 recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Use the lean R29 C4-first backbone, sharply isolate C5 and C6-paraffin blends, then add only profitable finishing columns. Step 1: validate the three high-value blends and measure costs.
R29 gives C4 $172.5M and C3 $53.8M. Its unsold BT and BBT are worth ~$610M and ~$725M, so sharper cuts can justify substantial extra cost. R38/R39 show B=90/6 still leaves C5 only 82-85%; stage/reflux increases alone are insufficient. Try B=110/10/3 and BB=90/8/4: current BB is already 92% C6 paraffin, so modest sharpening should cross 95%. Avoid broad full-purity trees and the low-value heavy branch.

note: Prune the uneconomic heavy-end column. This preserves all $752M/yr of blend revenue while eliminating $210M/yr of cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Lock in the profitable C3/C4/C5 plant, then test whether C6-paraffin recovery can beat its substantial separation cost; otherwise optimize the existing backbone. Step 1: remove the loss-making BB column.
Current B=110/10/3 gives the same sellable 95% C5 cut as R48's 120-stage column, so stages beyond 110 add no value. BB=90/8/4 leaves BBT only 84% C6 paraffin and BBB unsold while costing $210M/yr; deleting it raises reward from 0.269 to about 0.748. R49 shows excessive boil-up can destroy the C5 cut. Future tests should change the split strategy rather than simply increase reflux.

note: Sharpen B's C5/C6 cut with a moderate boil-up increase and more rectification, aiming to remove the residual pentanes that prevented the C6-paraffin blend from meeting 95%.
notebook:
PLAN: Lock in the profitable C3/C4/C5 plant, then recover the valuable C6-paraffin blend by first driving residual pentanes overhead in B; if that works, restore the BB splitter and optimize cost. Step 2: sharpen B's C5/C6 split.
Current 4-column plant earns 0.749. B=110/10/3 gives 95% C5 but leaves about 100 mol/s pentanes in BB, which limited BBT to 84-85% C6 even with a severe BB column. Increasing B stages alone (110 to 120) did nothing. R58 shows boil-up 4 fails, so use a moderate 3.4 with more stages/reflux. A clean BB feed should unlock roughly $1.25B/yr C6-paraffin revenue, easily justifying a sharper B and a BB column. Avoid root=40/2.5, which destroyed C4 and C3 sales.

note: Restore the proven 0.749 design after the overly aggressive B-column trial reduced both purity and profit.
notebook:
PLAN: Lock in the profitable C3/C4/C5 plant and improve its operating cost; pursue C6 recovery only if a modest splitter clears 95% purity, since the observed heavy-column costs are very high. Step 1: restore the proven 0.749 design after the failed 130/12/3.4 trial.
Current 4-column best earns 0.749 with B=110/10/3. R61 proves B=110/9/3 raises reward to 0.847 by cutting cost $5.6M/yr while increasing C5 revenue $54M/yr. The 130-stage trial lost C5 grade and cost more; R67's five-column C6 attempt costs $701.5M/yr and earns only 0.252. Restore the proven baseline now, then adopt R61's settings and test modest cost reductions. Avoid root=40/2.5 and large B reflux/boil-up changes.

note: Adopt R77's proven five-column design, which adds a profitable C6-paraffin blend to the established C3/C4/C5 backbone and raises reward to 1.981.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the proven five-column C3/C4/C5/C6-paraffin plant, then make only small changes to B and BB to improve recovery or cost without losing either blend grade.
R77 earns 1.981 with $1573.2M/yr revenue and $704.4M/yr cost. Its B=120/10/3.6 gives a $596.8M/yr C5 blend, and BB=120/10/5.0 gives a $750M/yr C6-paraffin blend. This dominates my pruned 0.749 plant. R69 shows B reflux 8 is best for the four-column version, but R77's extra C6 revenue justifies its cost. Avoid R78's high BB boil-up on the weaker B cut, which caused 8% n-pentane in BBT. Copy R77 exactly now; next test a modest B boil-up increase and/or lower BB boil-up to recover more C6 while limiting pentane carryover.

note: Combine R87's cheaper, higher-recovery BB column with the proven B boil-up increase to 3.7, targeting gains in both C5 and C6 blend revenue.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine the two independently successful refinements: R87's cheaper 110/9 BB column and the B boil-up 3.7 cut, then trim other costs only if both blends remain comfortably above 95%.
R87 scores 2.102: BB 110 stages/reflux 9 cuts cost $8.3M/yr and unexpectedly improves C6 recovery/value by $44.5M/yr. R81/R86 show B boil-up 3.7 adds $11M/yr C5 revenue for $4.6M/yr extra cost and reduces pentane in BB. Combining them should improve both C5 recovery and C6 purity. B 110/9 failed in R88, so retain B 120/10. Root and light train are already lean and should remain fixed.

PLAN: Start from R92's best 2.166 backbone, test whether B boil-up 3.7 adds C5 recovery without harming its superior C6 recovery, then trim the expensive root/B/BB columns cautiously.
R92 uses B 120/10/3.6 and BB 100/8.5/5: cost $691.2M/yr, revenue $1641.0M/yr. Its leaner BB recovers 704 mol/s C6 versus 678 in my design and is the current team best. B boil-up 3.7 previously added about $11M/yr C5 value for $4.6M/yr cost, so combining the independent gains is logical. Avoid B stage/reflux cuts: 110/9 previously failed. Heavy-end and ethane recovery have so far been uneconomic; preserve the four blend products.

note: Adopt the current best backbone and raise BB boil-up to 5.5, seeking substantial additional C6-paraffin recovery while monitoring its narrow purity margin.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R107's 2.234 backbone, then increase BB boil-up to recover more of the roughly 450 mol/s of valuable C6 paraffins currently lost to BBB; afterwards optimize BB reflux/boil-up and trim costs only if purity remains secure.
R107 is best: B 120/10/3.6 and BB 100/8/5, revenue 1666.4, cost 686.5. B boil-up 3.7 adds $11M C5 value but costs $4.6M and loses $15.7M C6 value, so 3.6 is superior. BB reflux 8 improves both cost and C6 recovery versus 8.5. BBT is 96% C6 paraffin, leaving only about 1% purity headroom, but 727 mol/s top versus 1185 mol/s feed paraffins means recovery is the larger opportunity. Test boil-up 5.5; heavier hydrocarbons may eventually contaminate the blend. Heavy-end and ethane recovery have been uneconomic; preserve C3/C4/C5 products.

note: Adopt R109's best 2.384 design and test one further BB boil-up increment, checking whether extra C6 recovery outweighs energy cost before purity collapses.

C4 splitting and heavy-end recovery have proven uneconomic. Test BB boil-up 6.5: recovery may rise another ~35 mol/s, but MCP/heavies could push BBT below 95%. If so, retain 6.0 and tune reflux instead. Preserve proven C3/C4/C5 cuts.
